speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I will be asking you some questions about the skin lesions you are presenting today to help determine their cause. To start, how long have you noticed these lesions, and have they changed in size, shape, or color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given your significant smoking history, age, and the non-healing nature of these lesions, I need to rule out malignancy. Can you describe the specific characteristics of the lesion on your finger, such as whether it is ulcerated, indurated, or bleeds easily?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the penis and left middle finger.

The clinical presentation of painless, non-healing, crusty lesions in a heavy smoker with African origin is highly suspicious for SCC, which can arise from chronic inflammatory conditions like syphilis or eczema (Marjolin's ulcer). Given the high suspicion of malignancy and the specific locations, immediate tissue sampling is required.

REQUEST TEST: Penile_biopsy and Left_middle_finger_biopsy
REQUEST IMAGES: Photos of penile lesion and finger lesion showing induration and ulceration.
